stem: A Massachusetts practitioner holds a valid professional license and an MCSR authorizing Schedule VI activity but does not yet have a DEA registration. The practitioner issues an otherwise valid prescription for an ordinary Schedule VI drug. Which registration statement is most accurate?

choices.text: The prescription is invalid because a DEA registration is required for every Massachusetts prescription drug, including Schedule VI.
The MCSR supports Schedule VI-only activity; DEA registration is needed when the practitioner conducts federally controlled Schedule II-V activity.
The MCSR is relevant only to Schedule I activity, so it does not authorize this Schedule VI prescription.
The pharmacy may place its DEA number on the prescription to cover the practitioner's missing federal registration.
Schedule VI prescribing requires neither an MCSR nor DEA registration when the drug is not federally controlled.

explanation.core_reasoning: A properly authorized Massachusetts practitioner may conduct Schedule VI-only activity with the MCSR even before obtaining a DEA registration.

choice_analysis.A: Massachusetts Schedule VI status alone does not require a federal DEA registration.
choice_analysis.B: The scenario fits the state-only registration distinction for Schedule VI activity.
choice_analysis.C: The MCSR governs Massachusetts controlled-substance activity beyond Schedule I.
choice_analysis.D: A pharmacy cannot supply prescriber registration authority by substituting its own DEA number.
choice_analysis.E: Schedule VI activity still requires the appropriate Massachusetts registration.

related_facts: Schedules II-V require both state and federal registrations.

reasoning_steps: Identify the drug as Massachusetts Schedule VI only
Apply MCSR-only practitioner authority for Schedule VI
